does: Works whole wheat flour and water into a soft, smooth dough with no yeast, then lets it rest. A rested dough is easy to roll thin and cooks into a soft, flexible flat bread.

intro.what: Atta dough brings whole wheat flour and water into a soft dough for thin flatbreads.
intro.why: It teaches you to balance softness and resting so the dough rolls readily instead of springing back.

how: Put the flour in a wide bowl with a little salt, and make a well.
Add warm water a little at a time, and bring the flour together with the fingers of one hand.
Press and fold the dough with the heel of the hand until it is smooth and soft, and no longer sticks to the bowl. It should be softer than a bread dough.
Rub the surface with a drop of oil, cover the bowl with a damp cloth, and leave the dough to rest.
Knead it briefly once more, then tear off equal balls and roll each one between the palms until it is smooth.

cues.text: The dough is soft as an earlobe, springs back slowly when pressed, and does not stick to the hands.
The surface is smooth and even, with no cracks, after the rest.

mistakes.mistake: Making the dough stiff, so that the breads turn hard and do not puff.
mistakes.fix: Add water until the dough is soft and just short of sticky.

mistakes.mistake: Skipping the rest, so that the dough springs back as it is rolled.
mistakes.fix: Cover it and leave it until it is relaxed.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the covered dough dry, so that a crust forms and shows as cracks and specks in the bread.
mistakes.fix: Cover it with a damp cloth or a plate.

quiz.question: Why rest the atta dough before rolling?
choices: To dry it into a firm crust.
To make it resist the rolling pin more strongly.
To let it relax so it rolls thin more easily.
quiz.because: Skipping the rest leaves dough that springs back instead of rolling out easily.

quiz.question: How do you bring in the water?
choices: Add it gradually while bringing the flour together.
Pour it all in before checking softness.
Keep the dough deliberately stiff from the start.
quiz.because: Gradual addition helps reach a soft dough rather than a stiff mixture that makes hard breads.

quiz.question: What feel matches the rested dough?
choices: Soft and smooth, springing back slowly without sticking.
A wet paste that cannot be shaped.
quiz.because: The dough should be soft and smooth rather than stiff or runny.

quiz.question: The dough forms a dry crust while resting. What would you change?
choices: Leave it uncovered to relax faster.
Dust heavily with flour before every rest.
Keep it covered with a damp cloth or plate.
quiz.because: Covering prevents the surface drying into cracks that carry into the bread.

variant_of.differs: The dough has no yeast and is worked only until it is smooth and soft, then left to rest. It is never worked until it turns elastic, and the softness comes from a high share of water.
